gaps: In the Blender front compare the polished skull mirrors the dark backdrop: head median V 0.16 against the concept's 0.63 (chest 0.69). The engine head reads lit (V 0.49). Putting only the skull back on aged brass measured compare V 0.29 but engine V 0.64, paler than the chest, so the skull stays polished.

The tail hangs to a key at z 0.45 m, where the concept's tail curls back up to a key at about 0.54 m; the head sits low on a forward neck rather than the concept's more upright one (both need bone moves).
Ruby saturation is still short of the concept: engine S 0.70 (idle), 0.76 (frozen), 0.74 (glow-close) against 0.86, and the rubies are seen mostly edge-on from the seat.

authorSelfScore.method: Author self-score on the reviewer's rubric: silhouette and proportions 22/30, signature features 22/25, surface detail and material read 12/20, colour and value 13/15, readability at play distance 10/10. Judged from spring-hound.fidelity-compare.jpg (orthographic EEVEE renders of the low-poly model at the concept's side, front and back angles, framed at the concept's own metres per pixel: side 1.2 m / 855 px, front and back 1.21 m / 875 px) side by side, and from the six in-engine shots in staging/engine (shared brass sets with the manifest tint, hound-glow through the runtime D11 glow). glow-close is now its own frame: idle through a 30 degree lens aimed at the upper body, where idle uses the 50 degree seat lens. Changes since the 74 review: the head has a stop (the brow drops 34 mm between y 0.752 and 0.772) and the muzzle top and underside follow the concept profile within 1 to 5 mm from y 0.758 to 0.859, so the mouth closes to a 14 mm gap; the needle-teeth rows became three upper and two lower teeth per side plus a fang at the front (none reaches the jaw: at least 4.2 mm clearance through attack). The eyes are 54 by 32 mm almonds standing 12.7 mm proud of their dark sockets: in the engine idle shot the eye glow is 155 px against the grille's 543 px (0.29, concept 0.22, was 26 against 418). Skull and jaw moved to polished brass and both brass normal strengths from 0.35 to 0.18, so the head and chest no longer read as crumpled foil; engine idle head median #7D5D3D (V 0.49) beside the chest's 0.62. The chest is narrower head-on (cuirass half-width 0.126 to 0.128 m), the haunch's back edge is 4 cm further forward and the gaskin bulges forward (shin-to-haunch plate overlap down from 90 to 71 triangles at rest, 136 to 129 at worst in death). The winding key is one flat bow with two round lobes, 56 mm across with 24 mm holes and 105 mm between centres, centred on the key bone (centroid 0.2 mm off the spin axis), and the tail is ten chunky segments. Rubies are a deeper crimson (#A00048) on a gunmetal slot at roughness 0.25 and metallic 0.8: engine median #541920 to #661B29 (hue 349 to 353, S 0.70 to 0.76, V 0.33 to 0.40) against the concept's #680F23 (S 0.86, V 0.41); joints stay warm black (#25170E). Engine whole-body brass hue 24 to 31. The compare lighting is the fixed warden-matched rig and was not tuned to the score.

independentScore.scorer: independent reviewer agent (separate from the authoring agent; did not build the model)

rubric.note: Up 1 from 20. Confirmed in the side compare crop (1470,270)-(1790,420): the brow now drops into a stop and the muzzle top and underside follow the concept's wedge, so the side head reads dog rather than rat. The hind leg now has the gaskin bulging forward and a sloped shin to a pointed hock (crop (930,450)-(1240,850)). Still off: head-on, which is the seat view, the muzzle is a round tube drooping from a bulbous domed cranium with an open jaw bar and a picket of spike teeth under it, confirmed at play distance in idle.jpg (upscaled crop (370,175)-(480,300)) and in glow-close.jpg; it reads anteater or rat, where the concept front is a narrow flat-topped wedge with a near-closed snarl. The chest is narrower than the last build but still wider than the concept head-on: model front silhouette 233 px against 212 at y 1270 and 205 against 178 at y 1220 of the compare (10 to 15 percent wider). The rump is a tall box, the back line runs level into it with no roach arch, the keel juts forward as a spike, and the neck still carries the head low and forward. The tail's hang is charged under signature features, not here.

Up 1 from 21. The eyes are fixed: idle.jpg eye glow is 169 px against the grille's 530 (ratio 0.32, mask HSV S over 0.4 and V over 0.8), against the concept front's 1284 to 3128 (ratio 0.41) with the same mask, and they read as large amber almonds at 2.6 m. The tail is now chunky segments. Grille as the single chest light, coil spine, neck coils, hinged jaw and shoulder and thigh rubies remain. Deductions: the winding key is one bow with round holes but in the side compare it still reads as two thin wire rings on a rod rather than the concept's solid flat plate with two small holes, so this is half a fix; the tail hangs straight down instead of curling up to present the key; the rubies are still small (69 red px in idle.jpg) and read dull in engine (median (87,29,35), per-pixel median HSV S 0.63) against the concept's (96,9,32), S 0.91. The open jaw is charged under silhouette, not here; these three items alone account for the 3 points off.

Up 1 from 13. The crumpled-foil hammered look in Blender and the suede head in engine are gone: skull and jaw now share the polished brass of the body. Paws now show toe divisions in idle.jpg. Still off: at the glow-close range the reduced normal reads as directional striations, so the chest looks like brushed wood grain and the neck coils like twisted rope (glow-close.jpg crop (310,190)-(500,580)); at play distance this mostly fades. Panel seams are still single thin black slits on the chest rather than the concept's bevelled, layered plate edges. The chest prow still carries a pale specular hotspot (idle.jpg chest (395,305)-(485,360) 90th percentile (237,207,171)). Legs below the forearm and gaskin remain plain plated cylinders.

Up 1 from 12. Judged on the engine shots (see method). sRGB medians over a warm-metal mask (max channel over 35, R over B plus 12, glow excluded): engine idle head (395,185)-(450,240) (126,93,62), hue 29, V 0.49, and chest (395,305)-(485,360) (131,97,62), hue 30, V 0.51, so the head is no longer a separate pale tan; concept side head (1030,70)-(1310,230) of the full-resolution sheet (116,81,55), hue 26, V 0.45, and concept front head (121,87,63), hue 25, V 0.47. Engine brass is about 4 to 5 deg yellower and slightly lighter than the concept. Glow matches: engine grille (243,185,74), hue 40, eyes (240,165,62), hue 35, against the concept grille (249,166,35), hue 37. Faults: the rubies are still under-saturated in engine (per-pixel median HSV S 0.60 to 0.66 across idle, glow-close, attack, hit and frozen, against the concept's 0.91 measured as the S of the median colour (96,9,32)), though the Blender compare ruby (128,9,41), S 0.93, hue 344, matches the concept, so the loss is in engine lighting and pixel size; the neck coils read paler and less saturated than the plates.

Up 1 from 8. The face now reads at 2.6 m: two large lit amber eyes plus the chest grille give the concept's glare and focal core (idle.jpg 555 glow px in total with S over 0.6 and V over 0.85, of which the eyes are 137). The hit pose stays readable (hit.jpg 582 glow px) and the body separates from the floor through its highlights rather than its median (idle chest median V 0.51 against floor V 0.53, but chest 90th percentile (237,207,171) against floor (137,100,75)) plus the dark joint bands. Deduction: head-on, the drooping tube muzzle and hanging jaw bar make the head read as a different animal before it reads greyhound, and the rubies are a few dark pixels from the seat. frozen.jpg shows no tint shift from idle; that is the roster-wide runtime ice tint and is not charged to the hound.

topFixes: Rebuild the head-on read, which is the seat view: narrow the domed cranium and turn the round tube muzzle into the concept's flat-topped tapering wedge, and close the jaw to a snarl so the spike teeth stop showing as a picket under a separate jaw bar (idle.jpg and glow-close.jpg).

Fix the remaining silhouette: narrow the shoulders head-on by about 10 percent (model 233 px against the concept's 212 at y 1270 of the compare), give the back a slight roach arch into a smaller, rounder rump, cut the keel spike back, raise the head on a more upright neck, and curl the tail up to the key.

Finish the signature details: make the winding key a solid flat plate with two small holes rather than two wire rings, enlarge and brighten the rubies so they read crimson in engine (per-pixel median S 0.60 to 0.66 now, concept 0.91), and replace the thin black slit seams with bevelled plate edges while softening the striated normal that reads as wood grain and rope up close.
independentScore.method: Independent re-score of the uncommitted pass-2 hound on 24ead5d with the same five-criterion rubric, re-checking every point of the 74 review against the new files rather than carrying it forward, and checking each of the author's claimed changes. Shape was judged on the fidelity compare (orthographic side, front and back at the concept's metres per pixel) with Pillow crops of the side head, the hind leg and tail, and the model front, plus front-silhouette widths measured against a background-difference mask in both front panels. Material and colour were weighted on the six engine shots, because the game is seen only through the three.js renderer, and the Blender compare's dark backdrop mirrors on the polished skull (Blender front head (400,990)-(540,1110) median V 0.17, against V 0.49 for the same head in engine idle.jpg), so Blender values were used only for shape and for the ruby's own colour. Colour is sRGB medians with HSV hue, saturation and value over a warm-metal mask (max channel over 35, R over B plus 12, glow excluded), glow as HSV S over 0.6 and V over 0.85 (eye-to-grille ratios with S over 0.4 and V over 0.8, applied identically to concept and engine), rubies as hue over 320 or under 5 with S over 0.35, in the pixel boxes given in the notes, kept off the floor. Concept boxes are in full-resolution 2752x1536 pixels. The death.jpg ruby median was not used (floor and edge contamination). The art bible and the P5 design notes (narrow head, two amber eyes, one amber chest core, ruby inlays) are a secondary check. Verified author claims: the stop and deeper muzzle, fewer larger teeth, large almond eye glow, skull on polished brass, gaskin forward with an angled hock, a single key bow with round holes, chunky tail segments and darker rubies. Partly true: the chest is narrower than before but still wider than the concept, and the key still reads as wire rings. The rise from 74 comes from the eyes, the side head profile, the hock and the unified head material; it stays below the bar on the head-on muzzle and jaw read and the remaining body proportions.
